text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The board of the IMF unanimously approved Egypt's economic reform programme for the next two years, which starts today. The fund agreed to inform the Paris Club of the approval, which automatically means the Paris Club will write off the last tranche of Egypt's debts to the club, which amount to $4 billion. Egypt will ask to be exempted from the interest which had accumulated on these debts before they were written off.
- King Fahd of Saudi Arabia received a telephone call yesterday from President Hosni Mubarak. They discussed bilateral relations and regional, Arab and international affairs.

- It has been decided to take a number of immediate measures to sort out 35 companies which have been in trouble for 21 years, in preparation for selling them or leasing them to anchor investors over the next two months. Public Enterprise Minister Atef Obeid said the measures include suspending any new investments, clearing the backlog of stock and repaying the debts of the companies, which amount to about 11 billion pounds ($3.2 billion) from the proceeds of the sale of the assets.
- Egypt will witness the partial eclipse of the sun today, starting at 4.25 p.m. (1425 GMT) and ending at 5.27 p.m.

- The Paris Club has told Egypt that it will write off the third tranche of debt, which is worth $4 billion. The official letter will arrive on Monday. The Club's agreement follows IMF approval of Egypt's economic reform programme.

- Supply and Trade Minister Ahmed Gueily announced that the government has set aside 3.5 billion pounds ($1 billion) to buy the whole cotton crop in case private companies remain reluctant to buy because the prices the government has set are higher than the export prices. He said that export prices keep rising, that so far Egypt has exported 308,000 qantars (15,400 tonnes) and that export prices are expected to rise in November and December. So far 1.7 million qantars (85,000 tonnes) have been picked and the crop is expected to be seven million qantars (350,000 tonnes). Public-sector textile companies will receive 4.5 million qantars (225,000 tonnes).
- French President Jacques Chirac will arrive in Egypt on October 25, during his Middle East tour.
- Egypt has asked the Paris Club to meet within the next few days to discuss writing off the third tranche of debt.
- Pakistan has invited President Mubarak to attend the Islamic sumit in Islamabad next year.
- Mobile phones will come into operation in 19 days. The dialling code will be 012 and the calls will cost 0.60 pounds ($0.18) a minute.
- The security forces have carried out a campaign in the hills east of the Nile in Sohag province to round up fugitive terrorists. The police obtained information.
